forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: No new data contradicts the prior collapse picture. USNI/Kpler: ~6 commercial transits/day April average, far below the 50/day threshold. IRGC Operational HQ issued a formal 'vast operational area' declaration May 30 (Jask to Siri Island), requiring IRGC Navy permission for all vessels. Trump's May 29 Situation Room meeting ended without a decision. Even an MOU signed June 3-5 cannot produce 50 consecutive transits/day within the remaining 9-day window to June 10 — mine-clearance, Lloyd's premium rebuild, and carrier-confidence recovery are physically incompatible with the timeline. Forecast is now at the schema probability floor (0.05). Flag for OBE review if Lloyd's premium and AIS transit count do not move by 2026-06-06.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor, IMF PortWatch (AIS lag confirmed ≤24h), UNCTAD Maritime Trade, or Lloyd's List reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. The 7-consecutive-day window must draw on confirmed AIS data with no more than 24h lag; a 48h+ data lag would make the June 10 resolution materially ambiguous. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Primary: IMF PortWatch AIS (lag ≤24h confirmed). Secondary: Hormuz Strait Monitor or Lloyd's List Intelligence. UNCTAD Maritime Trade Q2 2026 report lags by up to 8 weeks and cannot serve as primary resolution source before June 10 EOD. Minimum two independent confirming sources required.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse coverage: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. PGSA addendum (Judge 2026-05-19, confirmed 2026-05-31): third-country vessels transiting under Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime count ONLY IF ≥2 of IMF PortWatch/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls. Western insurer refusal of Hormuz coverage persists at horizon → sufficient condition for AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO regardless of reported transit counts.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's governing coalition lose its 61-seat Knesset majority (via defection, dissolution motion, or no-confidence) before the mandatory 2026-10-27 election date?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement — weekly cadence (Sundays only). Dissolution bill first reading scheduled June 1; result not available at report time. Full update Sunday 2026-06-07.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if a party-withdrawal letter is formally submitted to the Knesset Speaker and publicly confirmed by the departing party and acknowledged by the Speaker's office, OR if Netanyahu formally announces an early election date earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record plus Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel confirmation. Polling alone does not resolve. Reviewed weekly on Sundays only; no intra-week deltas allowed per Codex DA #12.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: counts as YES (majority lost). If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: counts as NO. A party-withdrawal letter formally submitted to the Knesset Speaker constitutes loss of coalition majority for resolution purposes without requiring a plenary roll-call vote, provided the withdrawal is publicly confirmed by the party and acknowledged by the Speaker's office. VOLUNTARY DISSOLUTION ADDENDUM (Judge 2026-05-31): a government-initiated dissolution bill passing all formal Knesset plenum readings by a majority vote counts as YES.

indicators.name: Smotrich or UTJ formally departs coalition (withdrawal letter to Speaker)
indicators.expected_effect: +10-20pp toward YES depending on which party departs.

indicators.name: Knesset dissolution bill second reading passes plenary
indicators.expected_effect: +30pp toward YES; dissolution bill passing final reading constitutes formal loss of majority under Voluntary Dissolution Addendum.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (containing both a Hormuz/ceasefire element AND an explicit nuclear negotiation framework component) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Trump's May 29 Situation Room meeting ended without a decision. He then sent revised language to Iran on May 31 targeting uranium retrieval mechanics and Hormuz wording. Fars published a same-day rebuttal stating Trump's post 'raised issues that contradict the provisions of the agreement's text.' Iranian MFA spokesperson Baghaei characterized US demands as 'not aligned with ongoing negotiations.' The ~3-day Iranian response window projects to ~June 3, leaving June 4-5 as the only available days for principal confirmation before horizon. Downward revision to 0.10.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official (Trump personally, or Secretary Rubio citing Trump's explicit written public authority) AND a named Iranian official (President Pezeshkian or his office, OR FM Araghchi with explicit Pezeshkian office endorsement within 72h) both publicly confirm a signed written framework containing both (a) a Hormuz/ceasefire element AND (b) an explicit nuclear negotiation framework component. Verbal 'agreement in principle' without document text or dual authentication does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Iranian state outlets (IRNA, Press TV, Fars) alone do NOT satisfy the Iranian principal confirmation requirement without independent corroboration from a Tier 1 non-state outlet. Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or US State Dept press release also resolves if dual-confirmed.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran FM Araghchi confirms but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. VP Vance confirmation alone, without Trump's explicit public authority delegation, does NOT trigger YES. A ceasefire MOU without nuclear framework component = NOT YES. 'Agreement in principle' phrasing without document text = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

US pattern of successive extensions established. Risks: Hezbollah non-participation, IDF strike violations (657 killed per Lebanese health ministry since truce), sovereignty disputes. forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire is either formally extended again OR replaced by a new framework agreement publicly confirmed by both Israeli and Lebanese governments (or US as guarantor) before EOD 2026-06-29. US State Department official statement, Israeli PM office, or Lebanese Presidency confirmation required.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Department official statement, Israeli PM office, or Lebanese Presidency confirmation. Reuters or AP corroboration required. Hezbollah unilateral ceasefire declarations alone do not resolve YES.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If talks are ongoing at EOD June 29 but no agreement text has been signed, resolve OPEN-AMBIGUOUS for up to 72 hours. If Hezbollah unilaterally declares end of ceasefire without Israeli response, resolve YES only if Israeli government confirms ongoing ceasefire with Lebanese state. Continued IDF strikes in south Lebanon at porous-truce intensity do NOT constitute ceasefire collapse for resolution purposes.
